items.text: A video received by Iran International shows protesters in Shahroud writing the slogan "Long live the Shah" on the wall opposite the Industrial University.

According to information received by Iran International, a number of students were arrested during the gathering on Saturday, 30 Aban in Kermanshah, protesting the killing of Sogand Sayadi. During this gathering, slogans including "Death to the dictator" were chanted.

In continuation of the Social Security retirees' protests, today, Sunday, 1 Azar, a group of them gathered in front of the Social Security building in Rasht. The retirees demanded a salary increase in line with inflation and living costs, as well as attention to their medical and supplementary insurance issues. They also held placards and chanted slogans demanding the release of teachers and political prisoners.

Milad Armoon and Navid Najaran, two prisoners sentenced to death in the "Ekbatān Town" case and detainees of the 1401 nationwide protests, were transferred to solitary confinement in Qezelhesar Prison in Karaj. Their death sentences were confirmed by the Supreme Court. They were moved to Suite 35, Unit 3 of Qezelhesar Prison.

According to videos received by Iran International, a group of students in Kermanshah took to the streets on Saturday, 30 Aban, protesting against the principal of Rezvan High School where "Sogand Sayadi" studies. According to reports, government forces beat them.

Javad Nekounam, head coach of Tractor, said in a press conference before the match against Al Wasl UAE that his team must enter the field with high focus and full mental readiness. He emphasized that the game is tough and the smarter team has a better chance for the desired result. Nekounam also mentioned the difficulties in reaching this stage and said every match is like a final for the team.

The Israeli army confirmed that it has joint plans with the US for a scenario of attack and resumption of war with Iran, and estimates that the time for Donald Trump's decision on action against Iran is near.

On the first of Azar, reports emerged of power outages in Mashhad, Varamin, Gonbad Kavus, and Lorestan. People complained about problems caused by the outages such as dark classrooms, gas cuts, and lack of internet and water. Some reports attributed the power outages to the sale of Iran's energy resources to neighboring countries.
A video sent to Iran International shows a one-week water cut and water supply by tanker in the village of Kuhabad, Taybad County, in Razavi Khorasan Province.

Mohammad Jafar Asadi, former deputy inspector of the Khatam al-Anbiya Central Headquarters, said that religious rulings may change over different periods. He added that jurists may have differing views on a subject. Asadi also said he is not a jurist and that answering this question is up to the jurists.

Mohammad Sharghi, detained during the protests of Dey 1404 and a security staff member at Mehrabad Airport in Tehran, has been sentenced to death by Branch 23 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court. He was sentenced for operational actions for hostile governments and membership in "oppositional" groups. His case is currently under review at Branch 9 of the Supreme Court.
A citizen sent a video to Iran International on Sunday, the first of Azar, showing the polluted air in Tehran and said: "We also have no electricity, water, or gas. This air is making us nauseous."

Fars News Agency reported the sentencing of Zahra Inchahdargahi, former head of the Gymnastics Federation, to two years of imprisonment and permanent dismissal from government services in a currency embezzlement case.

The murders of Parvaneh Eskandari and Dariush Forouhar on 22 November 1998 revealed state-organized killings. Shortly after, the bodies of Mohammad Mokhtari and Mohammad Pooyandeh were found with signs of strangulation. The Ministry of Intelligence admitted responsibility for 4 murders, but these killings have continued since the start of the Islamic Republic.

Milad Taqaddosi, deputy of treatment at Neyshabur University of Medical Sciences, announced that by noon on Sunday, 1 Azar, 72 people have been poisoned due to consumption of alcoholic beverages, and the number of victims has increased to 4. Mojtaba Mohebati, commander of Neyshabur police, reported the arrest of 12 suspects related to the production and distribution of toxic alcoholic drinks. Investigations to identify other individuals involved in this case continue.

Milad Farahani, former goalkeeper of several Premier League and First Division football teams in Iran, died this morning in a car accident on the Karaj to Rasht route. He played for teams including Paykan, Damash Gilan, Gol Gohar Sirjan, Saba Qom, Naft Tehran, Naft Masjed Soleyman, Shahr Khodro, Havadar, and Khoshe Talaei. His last football experience was with Mes Sungun Varzaghan.

The Iran Human Rights Organization in Norway confirmed on Saturday, 30 Aban, that Milad Armoon and Navid Najaran, two protesters of "Woman, Life, Freedom," are at imminent risk of execution. These two political prisoners were transferred to solitary confinement in Qezel Hesar prison. Iranian media reported on 3 Khordad that death sentences were issued for them, although they had previously been acquitted of the death penalty.
A citizen reported in a video to Iran International that the electricity in their area in Qods city was cut off without prior notice on Sunday, 1 Azar, and they have no electricity or gas.

Zahra Nosratpour, a citizen from Rasht, has been summoned to Lakan prison in the city to serve a prison sentence. She was previously sentenced by the judiciary to a total of four years, six months, and three days in prison, of which 31 months and 16 days are enforceable as the severest punishment against her.

Reports have emerged of Russian projectiles falling in Poland and violations of Finnish and Moldovan airspace. The NATO Secretary General, referring to escalating tensions on Europe's eastern borders, emphasized that this military alliance will defend Poland's territorial integrity.

The UK Maritime Trade Operations announced on Sunday, 1 Azar, that it received a report about an incident involving an oil tanker and military forces in the Sea of Oman. The organization urged vessels to review the latest maritime security information and remain alert to changes in the operational conditions of the area. The UK Maritime Trade Operations stated that relevant authorities have been informed of the incident and investigations are ongoing.

The UK Maritime Trade Operations Center reported that since 25 Aban, seven oil tankers have been attacked in the Strait of Hormuz, and the security threat level in this waterway remains "severe." Three oil tankers were targeted by unidentified projectiles on 29 and 30 Aban while exiting the Strait of Hormuz, with two tankers catching fire. The center also stated that attacks and harassment actions by the IRGC against commercial ships continue, and Iran's claim about oil tankers hitting naval mines has not been confirmed.
A citizen sent a video to Iran International reporting a 66% increase in hamburger prices over six months: "It has risen from 475,400 tomans in Esfand 1404 to 790,000 tomans in Mehr 1405."

Contrary to the Convention on the Rights of the Child, at least 1,642 female students from various cities in Iran were sent to operational areas in the south of the country as part of the so-called "Rahian-e Noor" tours, despite Iran's international commitments not to involve children in military activities.

The UK Maritime Trade Operations reported an incident between a tanker and military forces in the Sea of Oman. The organization did not provide further details and said investigations are ongoing. No information has been released about the ownership of the tanker or the identity of the military forces.
Amid the intensifying fuel crisis and rising transportation costs, truck drivers' strikes have expanded in various cities in Iran, and groups of Nissan and pickup drivers have also joined them.

President Trump spoke about the ongoing conflict with Iran and said he intends to resume attacks on Iran after the New Year if no agreement is reached. He said talks continue indirectly and described the Iranians as "professional tap dancers," adding that they keep talking.

Israeli media have reported that the US and Israel have drafted joint plans for a possible renewed attack on the Islamic Republic. At the same time, an attack on a civilian facility in Bahrain and its condemnation by Saudi Arabia, the UAE, and Qatar have increased concerns about escalating tensions.

Donald Trump, the President of the United States, announced that if no agreement is reached with the Islamic Republic, he intends to resume military attacks on Iran after the start of the new Gregorian year. He said indirect talks with the Islamic Republic continue but criticized the negotiation process. Trump also warned that if Iranian vessels attempt to break the US naval blockade, all of them will go to the bottom of the sea.
A new wave of truck drivers' strikes in Iran has been reported. Protests and anti-government graffiti continue. This news was reported by Iran International.
A video received by Iran International shows the installation of a poster with the design of the Lion and Sun flag in support of the Abdanan protests on a wall in southern Tehran.

The tanker tracking institute, Tanker Trackers, denied claims of an Iranian tanker named "Khatshkan" moving towards the Sea of Oman and stated that such a tanker does not exist. These reports emerged while the US naval blockade has entered its 130th day and the Islamic Republic's oil exports face severe restrictions.

The death sentence of a prisoner accused of murder was carried out on Tuesday, 26 Aban, at the Central Prison of Karaj. Additionally, three death row convicts in Mazandaran province and a woman in a case in Tehran were released from the gallows due to the forgiveness of the victims' families.

Ali Kowsari, deputy of education at the Basij Mostazafan Organization, said that simultaneously with the 5th of Azar, the anniversary of the Basij's establishment, the "Janfadaian" training program will start in 110 locations across the country. He added that the Basij is planning to build field training bases near several historical sites including Persepolis, Arg-e Bam, Chogha Zanbil Ziggurat in Shush, and Ferdowsi's tomb, and the execution of some of these projects will begin in the coming days.

Planned power outages began on Sunday, the first of Azar, in various regions of Iran. Tavanir Company announced new restrictions on electricity supply for residential and commercial customers due to fuel shortages at power plants. The outages may last up to two hours every two days and in some areas up to two hours per day.

More than 100 service workers of Yasuj Municipality reported non-payment of three months of their salaries. Workers of the machinery unit of Travers Karaj company protested against wage, insurance problems, and lack of job security. Also, a group of Social Security retirees reported delays in the payment of their November pensions.

Mohammad Maljo, an economist and economic researcher, has been sentenced to one year of imprisonment by a judicial authority. His court sessions were held in early Tir and mid-Mehr 1405. The report prepared by the interrogators of the IRGC Intelligence Organization was the basis for issuing the one-year imprisonment sentence against him.

Liverpool football team defeated Manchester United 4-0 in the 11th week of the English Premier League at Anfield stadium. Lenny Yaro's red card in the eighth minute left United with 10 players from the start of the match. Mauricio Pochettino began his first match as Manchester United coach with a heavy defeat.
Yadollah Motaei, a citizen from Dehgolan imprisoned in Qorveh prison, was sentenced to 39 months and two days in prison by the judiciary of Dehgolan county.

The number of detainees in Darreh Shahr increased to 6. Including two other citizens named Mohammad Olad and Hamid Mirzaei, the number of detainees on Friday, 29 Aban in Darreh Shahr county reached six. Earlier, the arrest of four other citizens named Amir Garavand, Ali Vali, Aryan Imani, and Erfan Esmaeili was reported.
A citizen sent a video to Iran International on Sunday, the first of Azar, showing mazut burning at the Shazand power plant in Arak and severe air pollution.

Mehdi Mahdavi-Azad said in the Cheshmandaz program that the truck drivers' strike in 1404 expanded to at least 150 cities, but censorship, repression, and security arrests prevented its continuation and expansion.

Two citizens were arrested by the IRGC intelligence forces due to activities in cyberspace. A video of their forced confessions has been released, but the conditions under which it was recorded are unclear.

Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, the Speaker of the Parliament, said that energy reform is the "most urgent and important issue" of the country both during peace and today, but gasoline "is not worth reforming at all" and should be the "last issue." He added that gasoline accounts for 9% and gas 73% of energy consumption in Iran, and solving the gas issue "can solve the people's and government's problems" and bring economic security and social resilience.

The human rights group Halvash reported on Sunday, 1 Azar, with a video that hundreds of heavy vehicles have been stuck in line over the past few days at the Rimdan border crossing in Sistan and Baluchestan province. Drivers reported disorder in queue management, lack of welfare facilities, and the risk of spoilage of fruit and vegetable shipments.

Nine months after Khamenei's removal, a senior researcher of the Resistance Front revealed Mossad's infiltration at the highest level of the Islamic Republic. According to him, Mossad, by capturing the regime's intelligence institutions, became the source of information for Iran's leaders about Israel and was able to shape their narrative in its favor.

According to the monthly report of Aban 1405 by the Statistics Department of the Human Rights Activists in Iran, at least 75 prisoners including one woman were executed in Iran. During this period, 31 death sentences including one for a woman were issued and seven death sentences were confirmed by the Supreme Court. Notable cases include the execution of several detainees from the December 1404 protests and the issuance of a death sentence against Amirhossein Mousavi, a political prisoner in Evin prison.

Alireza Hosseinali-zadeh, the police commander of Mashhad, announced that in an attack by two individuals on police officers on Emamat Boulevard in this city, three officers were superficially injured. The police shot both attackers and one of them died after being transferred to the hospital. This incident occurred on Sunday evening at the beginning of Emamat Boulevard in Mashhad.
A video received by Iran International shows protesters in Dehloran writing the slogan "Salute to Abdanan" on a public wall in support of the protesting people of Abdanan.

Officials from the medical universities of Nishapur and Shiraz reported that about 150 people were poisoned due to consuming counterfeit alcoholic beverages in Nishapur, Shiraz, and Marvdasht. So far, five people have died, one person has suffered brain death, and several poisoned individuals are hospitalized in intensive care units. In Nishapur, 120 people were poisoned and four have died, while in Shiraz and Marvdasht about 30 people were poisoned and one person has died.

The human rights website Harana reported that Mohammad Sharghi, a security staff member at Mehrabad Airport and detainee of the January protests, has been sentenced to death by Branch 23 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court.

A presenter on the Islamic Republic's state TV questioned Bahrain's independence during a live program on Channel 3, saying they would like to declare Bahrain as Iran's 32nd province. He mocked Bahrain's request for action against the Islamic Republic, saying Bahrain's bigger ally has come and could do nothing. Bahrain's Foreign Ministry had earlier condemned the Islamic Republic's air attack on a non-military industrial complex and called for UN Security Council action.
A citizen sent a video to Iran International showing pomegranate sellers' vans on Saveh road and said that municipality officers shut down their business and took their scales.
Milad Farahani, former goalkeeper of several Premier League and First Division football teams in Iran, died on Sunday morning due to a traffic accident on the road from Karaj to Rasht.
The football teams Foolad Khuzestan and Sepahan Isfahan drew 2-2 in the 13th week of the Iranian Premier League. This match was one of the most beautiful games of this season of Iranian football.

Morad Veysi, senior analyst at Iran International, said Trump says if no agreement is reached, attacks will resume after the New Year. He added Trump's threat is serious but the attack could start earlier and unexpectedly. Veysi asked if this means the Islamic Republic is safe from a US attack for the next forty days.

A group of Iranians gathered in front of the federal building in Los Angeles and condemned the continued suppression of citizens in support of the Abdanan protests. This was reported by Niloufar Mansouri, a reporter for Iran International, along with her interview with participants in this gathering.

Trump predicted that if Democrats win the November 3 midterm elections, stock markets would crash and the Islamic Republic of Iran would become more aggressive in its attacks. He said Iran launched more drones and missiles last week than at any time in over a year, but all were shot down without causing damage. Trump also claimed that both Democrats and Iran fought to keep oil prices high, but since the election, oil prices have fallen sharply.

Donald Trump, the President of the United States, announced on the evening of Sunday, 1 Azar, that the Islamic Republic has killed 81,000 protesters up to this date. He said that Iran has launched more drones and missiles in the past week than at any time in over a year, and all were intercepted and shot down. Trump also accused the Democrats and the Islamic Republic of trying to keep oil prices high and described the recent election as "very strange."

Farzad Talakesh, Secretary General of the Iran Poultry Federation, stated that the reasonable price for a tray of eggs for consumers is between 700,000 to 750,000 tomans and the price of chicken meat is about 400,000 to 430,000 tomans per kilogram. He also said that chicken meat consumption has decreased by more than 25 percent compared to the same period.

Sohrab Bakhtiyari-Zadeh, Esteghlal's head coach, resigned last week in protest of the club's neglect of the senior football team, but returned to training two days later. Esteghlal's managers have formed many teams in non-football sports and recruited many low-quality players in the past two seasons. This was discussed in a conversation between Mazdak Mirzaei, Mohammad Taghavi, and Raha Pourbakhsh on the Hat-trick program.

Agence France-Presse reported that Bahrain's Ministry of Interior announced on Sunday, Azar 1, that in Iran's Saturday attack on a civilian industrial facility in the country, two people were injured, one of whom is in critical condition. According to Bahrain's Ministry of Interior, one of the injured is a Bahraini citizen with a disability who is stable, and the other is a Pakistani national in critical condition. The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps announced on Saturday evening that it targeted US Patriot air defense systems at Bahrain bases with missiles and drones.

Reza Arab, a political analyst, said Washington and Israel believe the economic blockade is yielding results and intend to continue this pressure. He added that the goal of the US and Israel might be to coincide the intensification of economic pressure with the expansion of protests in Iran, and Trump tries to avoid deploying ground troops. Arab also said if economic pressure increases and the Islamic Republic feels unable to control protests, it may risk direct confrontation with the US and even send warships to break the blockade.

Amir Giti, a member of the Iran International editorial team, referred to Donald Trump's statements about the killing of 81,000 protesters in Iran by the Islamic Republic and the increase in drone and missile attacks. He said Trump, while supporting the protests of the Iranian people, continues military, economic, and political pressures on the Islamic Republic and also gives diplomacy a chance. He emphasized that the victory of the Democrats in the US midterm elections does not necessarily lead to a reduction in pressure on the Islamic Republic, because the Democrats also have hardline positions against Tehran's nuclear program.

Pegah Bani-Hashemi, a senior legal researcher at the University of Chicago, said that the issuance of different sentences in the criminal court and the revolutionary court indicates a lack of judicial independence and its susceptibility to political considerations. She emphasized that in conditions where the attribution of murder to these individuals is not proven, using the charge of moharebeh for issuing the death penalty raises serious legal questions. Bani-Hashemi stated that the realization of the charge of moharebeh requires specific legal conditions, including the use of weapons, while these individuals did not have weapons at the time of the incident.

Shokouh Mirzadegi, founder of the Pasargad Foundation, said the Islamic Republic uses the country's cultural heritage as a tool to threaten people. She compared this action to the Nazi forces' threats against historical monuments in Paris and called for an immediate response from UNESCO and international heritage protection organizations. Mirzadegi emphasized that cultural activists and the Iranian people must act to prevent damage to national monuments.

Abbas Goudarzi, spokesperson of the Parliament's presidium, said that negotiation with the US has no basis because the US attacks in the middle of negotiations and only understands the language of force. He added that fulfilling the seven conditions between Iran and the US is the main condition. Goudarzi also said that with reliance on God and perseverance, we will be the final victors, and anyone who undermines the nation's resistance due to trust in the enemy will not be forgiven by God.

Mohammad Qaedi, an international relations lecturer, said the explosion on a Russian ship at the Benghazi naval base in Libya, likely caused by a drone attack, weakens Russia's military credibility in Africa. He added that Russia has expanded its influence in African countries through the Wagner group and security agreements, competing with the US, France, and China. Qaedi said Moscow's inability to protect its ships in eastern Libya questions Russia's security commitments to its African allies.

Abolfazl Aboutorabi, a member of the Parliament's Councils Commission, said that the passage of oil through the southern route of the Strait of Hormuz has significantly decreased. He also stated that the Islamic Republic hits about 10 large violating oil tankers daily on average. Aboutorabi added that the conditions of the Strait of Hormuz will not return to pre-war times and that the Islamic Republic will demonstrate its control over the strait more than before to its enemies.

Hossein Ghazian, a sociologist, commented on the poisoning of about 150 people due to consumption of alcoholic beverages in Shiraz, Marvdasht, and Nishapur, which resulted in the death of five people and one brain death. He said the Islamic Republic focuses on the ideological prohibition of alcohol consumption instead of protecting citizens' lives. Ghazian added that the government tries harder to combat alcohol consumption than to prevent the production of counterfeit drinks and effectively ignores its responsibility towards consumers.

Australia's ABC network reported that despite the ban on women dancing in public places and the risk of arrest and imprisonment in Iran, a group of young ballet dancers continue their artistic activities secretly. According to the report, these artists practice in hidden homes and studios, and an underground network called "Iran Dancers" supports them with the cooperation of coaches abroad. These dancers hope to one day perform freely in Iran without fear of arrest and government restrictions.

According to the monthly report of Aban 1405 by the Statistics Department of the Human Rights Activists in Iran, at least 50 deaths due to lack of safety in the workplace and 71 cases of worker injuries were recorded this month. Additionally, 1899 cases of dismissal and workforce adjustment, 497 cases of job uncertainty, and 37 months of wage arrears were recorded. In this month, 90 gatherings and seven labor and union strikes, four arrests, and a total of 72 months of suspended imprisonment for six people were recorded.

Pirhossein Kolivand, head of the Red Crescent Society, said that with Hassan Nasrallah's approval, 500 of the most critical injured from the Hezbollah pager incident in Lebanon were transferred to Iran, and 85% of these injured improved in Iran. Some of these individuals had lost their sight or some body parts, and during the flight, some received blood transfusions. Kolivand added that examinations of Iranian patients and elective surgeries were not delayed at all.

A video sent to Iran International shows that truck drivers in Baharestan, Isfahan province, went on strike on Sunday, the first of Azar. Earlier, a video of truck drivers' strike in Shiraz was also published on the same day.

Hossein Alizadeh, a former diplomat and international affairs analyst, said the agreement between Azerbaijan and Armenia on the Trump corridor could shift the geopolitical balance of the South Caucasus in favor of the US, Turkey, and Azerbaijan and to the detriment of Tehran and Moscow's influence.

The 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference, known as COP 31, ended on Sunday in Antalya, Turkey, without reaching a comprehensive political agreement. The meeting, which extended two days beyond the scheduled time, became the longest climate conference in history.

Carlos Alcaraz, after a four-month wrist injury break, became the youngest man in history to win all four Grand Slams and the ATP Finals by defeating Alexander Zverev in Turin. The 23-year-old Spanish star won the Australian Open in January and then the season-ending tournament in Turin ten months later. After returning from injury, he recorded 21 wins in 22 matches and claimed four major titles.

Ahmad Bakhshaish Ardestani, a member of the National Security Commission of the Parliament, said that the range of Iran's missiles has increased from 2,000 kilometers to 4,500 kilometers, and the young leader has declared that the missiles should be precise and pinpoint. He also said that Qatar can no longer be a good mediator because it wants to play the role of mediator while condemning Iran. Bakhshaish Ardestani criticized Masoud Pezeshkian and said he should learn from the President of Ukraine, whose country has been at war for four years but does not engage in such actions.
A citizen sent a video to Iran International showing severe air pollution in Tehran on Tuesday, the second of Azar, and crying said: "Curse the Islamic Republic. What day have you brought us to?"

The Iranian national beach soccer team secured first place in Group B of the 2026 Asian Beach Soccer Championship by defeating Lebanon 7-2 and advanced to the next stage with their third consecutive win. Mohahed Mohammadpour, Mohammad Masoumi-Zadeh, and Mohammad Ali Mokhtari each scored twice, and Seyed Mehdi Mirjalili scored another goal. Iran had already secured advancement by winning against Afghanistan and Vietnam.

Esmaeil Baqaei, spokesperson for the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, called the condemnation of the Islamic Republic's actions by Germany and Qatar "rejected and unacceptable" and said Qatar's statements were "unexpected". He also announced the summoning of Qatar's chargé d'affaires to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the delivery of the Islamic Republic's protest. Baqaei said about the Qatari Prime Minister's trip to Washington that stopping the war on all fronts is an integral part of any agreement and this demand shows the Islamic Republic's responsibility for regional security and stability.
Fatemeh (Hasti) Varamziar, a citizen from Ilam, was arrested on Sunday, 1 Azar, after being summoned and referring to the prosecutor's office of this city and was transferred to Ilam prison.

Pirhossein Kolivand, head of the Red Crescent, said that during the California wildfires he sent a letter to the US offering to send forces to help. He added that the Americans responded that they did not need forces and asked for financial assistance instead.

Amin Soltani, former board member of Esteghlal Khuzestan club, confirmed that inappropriate messages were exchanged between a youth team coach and several players. He said that the documents of this case were submitted to supervisory bodies and the authenticity of the messages was confirmed by these bodies. Soltani added that efforts were made for the coach to resign, but this did not happen and the issue escalated.

Israeli media reported that Israeli military intelligence agencies have warned Benjamin Netanyahu that a unilateral attack on the Islamic Republic could lead to the expansion of the war to Lebanon, Syria, and Gaza. Channels 11 and 12 and the Walla website reported that the White House prefers to wait at least another week to assess the impact of the siege.

Fatemeh Manouchehri, a national para-athletics athlete and bronze medalist at the Asian and Oceania Championships, died on Tuesday, 2 Azar, after about a month in a coma. Fars News Agency reported that the cause of her coma was cardiac arrest. Manouchehri competed in shot put and placed sixth in this event at the Hangzhou Para Asian Games in China.

On Monday, 2 Azar, a group of retired telecommunications workers held a protest in the cities of Kermanshah and Sanandaj. The retirees demanded the implementation of regulation 89/24, enforcement of Administrative Justice Court ruling 9235, salary adjustments, and attention to their other demands.

Mohammad Reza Naqdi, senior advisor to the commander of the IRGC, said the US does not have the capability for a ground attack on the Islamic Republic and that a naval attack would involve significant risks and costs. He added that the only military option available to the US is airstrikes, which would be met with reciprocal responses. Naqdi also said US politicians hope economic pressures will cause public despair and weaken officials' resolve, but officials and military forces will not retreat under these pressures.

According to information received by Iran International, the family of Alireza Raeisi, an executed protester, was forced by security agents to cover the poem engraved on his tombstone in the deserts of Anarak in Isfahan province with black spray. The poem on his tombstone praised those who left the world with dignity and embraced truth. Alireza Raeisi, one of the detainees in the so-called "Alikhani Square" case in Isfahan, was executed on 13 Mehr.

Student councils of 31 universities in the country issued a joint statement declaring they will not remain silent against "fabrication of cases" and disciplinary actions against student representatives. The statement mentioned the issuance of a four-semester suspension for Pejman Nasiri and called for the cancellation of this sentence and the guarantee of the independence of student councils. Reports of case formations and pressure on council members at various universities have also been received.

Lamine Yamal, Barcelona star, will miss Wednesday night's match against Sabah in the UEFA Champions League due to a minor discomfort in his right ankle. The club announced that he will not participate in this game as a precaution and is expected to return next Sunday against Deportivo La Coruña. Yamal played the full 90 minutes in the previous match but the medical staff decided not to field him in the upcoming game to prevent worsening the issue.

Lida Pirasteh, a Bahá'í citizen residing in Semnan, was summoned and interrogated by the Intelligence Department of this city for the second time. This Bahá'í citizen was also summoned and interrogated by this security agency yesterday. This news was reported by Harana News Agency.

Masoud Pezeshkian, head of the Islamic Republic government, said at an event that the US and Europe cannot overthrow us unless we overthrow ourselves. He emphasized the need for interaction and kindness in conversations and added that if God's and the Imam's orders are followed, all problems will be solved.

Ali Hossein Ghazizadeh, a member of Iran International's editorial board, referred to statements by Mostafa Izadi, deputy commander of the IRGC, about the readiness of the IRGC and Basij to confront internal unrest. He said the Islamic Republic's main concern is the return of widespread protests to the streets. He considered the claim of about 450,000 Basij members participating in Tehran IRGC programs exaggerated and said the government tries to intimidate people before new protests by announcing such figures and repeated threats.

The strike of truck drivers and drivers in several cities in Iran entered its second day on Monday, 2 Azar, amid the intensification of the fuel crisis and worsening economic conditions. The Union of Truck Drivers' Associations announced that the strike will continue until the drivers' demands are met, and Nissan drivers have also joined the strike.

A two-day meeting of Afghan women hosted by the Spanish Ministry of Foreign Affairs began on Sunday, 1 Azar, in Madrid. At the same time, the campaign "One Million Voices for Afghan Women and Girls" has called for concrete action by the international community to secure women's rights.

A citizen sent a video to Iran International showing widespread power outages on Sunday, the first of Azar, and said they have no electricity and all people are living under pressure, but they do not lose hope.

The Iranian women's national handball team defeated Hong Kong 33-16 in their first match at the Asian Championship hosted by Kazakhstan. Fatemeh Khalili, the goalkeeper of the Iranian national team, was named the best player on the field. Iran is in Group A with Japan, China, Thailand, and Hong Kong, and will face China tomorrow, November 24, at 15:30.

Bild newspaper reported that about 450 schools across Germany received bomb threat emails on Monday morning. German police stated that these messages with identical text were sent to hundreds of schools and investigations have started to identify the senders. Police said the threats are not currently considered serious and a case has been opened on charges of "disturbing public order through threats of committing a crime."

Ebrahim Azizi, head of the National Security Commission of the Parliament, said on Tuesday, 2 Azar, that the Islamic Republic is "not susceptible to siege." He added: "We will take any action to break the siege."

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic summoned the Qatari chargé d'affaires in the absence of the country's ambassador in protest against the joint statement by Qatar and Germany against the Islamic Republic. Esmail Baghayi, spokesperson for the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, called Qatar's position on the nuclear file and maritime security "surprising and regrettable." Qatar and Germany condemned missile attacks and threats to shipping in the Strait of Hormuz in their joint statement.

Shahrouz Sadidi, a resident of Sabzevar, remains in detention without a clear status despite 55 days passing since his arrest. He was previously held in quarantine ward and has now been transferred to the general ward. Judicial officials have not provided a clear explanation regarding the handling of his case, and his lawyers have not been able to access his file.
A second-grade student in the village of Siyahkaleh in Dorud county says in a video that the Molavi school teacher in this village broke his foot because he did not write his homework.

Masoud Pezeshkian, head of the Islamic Republic government, responded to criticisms of corruption among government officials by saying those who make such claims should closely observe the lives of these individuals. He added that some of those who were killed had simple lives and even one of the commanders did not have a house of his own.

Videos received show that retirees in Kermanshah, Isfahan, and Sanandaj came to the streets on Tuesday, 2 Azar, to demand their rights and called the "Execution of Imam Khomeini's Order Headquarters" and the "Cooperative Foundation of the IRGC" "usurpers."

Amnesty International has issued a public call for protesters, families of the killed, eyewitnesses, healthcare workers, and others with information about the January 2026 protests to participate in documenting these events. Amnesty stated that many aspects of the January killings still need precise documentation and that recording "patterns of killing and injuring protesters" is important for increasing global attention and enabling judicial prosecution of Islamic Republic officials. The call especially asks those with information about the events of January 9 and 10 in Tehran, Isfahan, Rasht, Mashhad, and Shiraz to contact the organization via secure messengers, assuring confidentiality of sources and contacts.

Ali Ahmadi, a retired teacher living in Nurabad Mamasani, has been detained in Adelabad Prison in Shiraz for over eight months. His legal case was recently transferred from Branch 10 of Shiraz Prosecutor's Office to Branch 2 of Nurabad Mamasani Prosecutor's Office. According to Harana News Agency, Ali Ahmadi remains in detention.

Mostafa Nili, a lawyer, announced that the sentence of 74 lashes for Parasto Ahmadi and four others involved in the so-called "hypothetical concert" at the historic Dirgachin Caravanserai in Qom has been carried out. After the sentence was finalized and the case sent to enforcement, these individuals appeared at the Qom prosecutor's office and the lash punishment was executed. The sentence was issued on charges of "violating public decency through producing and publishing obscene and immoral content in cyberspace."

Ukraine released new images of its naval drones attacking a Russian warship and sinking it in the port of Benghazi, Libya. This operation has been described as one of the most important attacks during the Ukraine war.

The ceremony marking the 28th anniversary of the murder of Dariush and Parvaneh Forouhar was held on Sunday evening under threats from security and judicial institutions at the Forouhar family residence in Tehran. Morteza Kazemian explains the case of the political murders in autumn 1377 and the brutal killing of the Forouhars, and speaks about the continuation of intimidation by the Islamic Republic, suppression of opponents in Iran, and the deepening divide between the nation and the government.

A source familiar with the situation of Bahá'í citizens in Iran told Iran International that Ministry of Intelligence agents arrested Kimia Mostafavi, Roha Imani, and Hooman Imani, three Bahá'í citizens, in Kerman and summoned Leida Pirasteh, a Bahá'í citizen residing in Semnan, for the second consecutive day to the Intelligence Department. Mostafavi and Roha Imani were arrested on the night of Sunday, 1 Azar, and Hooman Imani on the morning of Monday, 2 Azar. After searching their homes and confiscating personal belongings, agents transferred them to an unknown location.

Slogan writing is an important part of the protests that have intensified in Iran these days. Videos received by Iran International show the writing of the slogan "Long live the Shah" on the walls of public passages in the city of Rasht.

It was announced by Shams Azar Qazvin club that Voria Ghafouri, former captain of Esteghlal, was appointed as the new head coach of the club. Ghafouri replaces Vahid Rezaei, who was dismissed from coaching on the first of Azar. Shams Azar has had poor results in the current season of the Iranian Premier League and is currently in seventeenth place in the standings.

Today, Monday, a group of essential goods importers held a protest in front of the Ministry of Agriculture Jihad building. The protest was against the failure to fulfill promises and a 19-month delay in paying their foreign currency claims.

The Lebanese army announced that it has discovered and seized more than 260 kilograms of explosives smuggled from Syrian territory in the Bekaa region. The routes for transferring weapons from the Islamic Republic to Hezbollah in Lebanon are becoming increasingly restricted. After the fall of Bashar al-Assad, the route for transferring weapons and explosives from Syria to Lebanon was cut off, and Beirut and Damascus cooperate in pursuing arms smugglers.

The official media of Mojtaba Khamenei, leader of the Islamic Republic, published a threatening design against Jewish identity and religious symbols ahead of the Hanukkah festival. Ben Sabti, a researcher on Iran and Israel issues, said the Islamic Republic has resorted to old propaganda to mobilize Iranian people who oppose the regime. He added this propaganda is for domestic consumption but has lost its effectiveness because the Iranian people have friendly relations with Israel and its people.

Iranian media reported that Gholamreza Nikkhah, a veteran cinema and television actor, died on Tuesday, 2 Azar, due to a heart attack. Nikkhah was born on 1 Farvardin 1327 and acted in various films and series. He had roles in comedy series and reality shows.

Ahmadreza Radan, the commander of the national police, said at a war-related ceremony that they assure everyone they will identify and suppress any sedition before it starts and will not allow it to emerge. He added that a country known historically for using dirty bombs wants to accuse our country of using these bombs. Radan also said that in the police domain, they have taken the leader's orders as their guiding principle.

Today, Monday, 2 Azar, a number of employees of the Khorasan Razavi Welfare Organization held a protest in front of the Welfare Organization's headquarters in Mashhad, demanding attention to their demands, including the adjustment of their wages and job benefits.

Mohammad Esmaeili Alafi, a lawyer and member of the East Azerbaijan Bar Association, was released from Tabriz prison on Saturday, 30 Aban, after posting a bail of five billion tomans. This was reported by the HRANA news agency.

A released video shows that the symbol of the map of Iran installed on the eternal grave of Meysam Abid was destroyed overnight. Meysam Abid was wounded by a gunshot in Fardis on 18 Dey and died in the hospital on 5 Bahman of the same year.

Alireza Mansourian and his Iranian assistants will miss Al-Zawraa's match against Al-Riffa due to Bahrain visa denial. The Iraqi club has requested to move the match to a third country. Al-Zawraa boycotted the pre-match coordination meeting in protest of the visa denial for technical staff members.

The family of Alireza Raeisi was forced by security agents to erase a commemorative poem from his tombstone. Additionally, the tombstone of Meysam Aybed, a 29-year-old killed in the December protests, was destroyed overnight in Malmir village. This information was reported to Iran International.

Benjamin Netanyahu, Prime Minister of Israel, responded to Gadi Eisenkot's remarks about the absence of an immediate threat from Iran by saying that the threat from Iran against Israel is immediate. Netanyahu called for the formation of a national unity government including ultra-Orthodox Jewish parties and emphasized the need to reach an agreement with these parties on Israel's Jewish identity and military service.
Today, continuing the gatherings of telecommunications retirees; some of these retirees in the cities of Isfahan and Tehran also held protest gatherings demanding attention to their demands.

Mostafa Nili, a lawyer, said that the sentence of 74 lashes for Parasto Ahmadi and four of her associates in the historic Dirgachin caravanserai was carried out today, Monday, 2 Azar 1405, at the Qom Prosecutor's Office. According to Nili, these individuals appeared at the enforcement unit of the Qom Prosecutor's Office after the sentence was confirmed by the appeals court, and the lash sentence for all five was executed.

Players and referees of Serie A teams wore red marks on their faces in the twelfth week matches to show support against violence towards women. The campaign, titled "Red Card to Violence," was held on November 25, the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women. The Serie A football league president said the campaign was a symbol inviting intervention against violence.
